transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?
My head’s been feeling foggy lately. I’ve been making little mistakes in my client notes and forgetting what I was about to do, and that’s not really like me.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?
My sleep’s been pretty all over the place. Some nights I’m lying there thinking about family stuff, and other times I wake up before my alarm and can’t really get back to sleep.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah. Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and flat.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low mood and the brain fog—has it been going on for two weeks or more?
I think it really started after my uncle died, about two weeks ago.
Even when you're not actively thinking about your uncle, do you still feel that same heavy, sad, foggy feeling throughout the day, or does it mostly come and go when something reminds you of him?
It’s there most of the day, even when I’m not thinking about him. I wake up feeling heavy and empty, and I can do my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and flat.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities or things you used to enjoy, even ones unrelated to your uncle?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change in that specifically—I’ve mostly just been feeling sad and kind of flat.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over the past two weeks?
I haven’t really noticed any change in my appetite or weight, no.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless or excessively guilty about things, or any thoughts of death or that you'd be better off not being here?
I’m not planning to hurt myself. But some mornings I do think… it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy nearly every day, even when you've had enough rest?
Yeah. Even on days when I don’t do much, I feel worn out physically. Things like helping a client shower or carrying groceries take a lot more out of me than they usually should.

Are there any moments during the day, even brief ones, when you feel more like your usual self or can enjoy something, or does the sad, flat feeling stay constant no matter what's happening around you?
It’s pretty constant. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling, and I can get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I’m still just sad and flat.
Has this sadness and fatigue affected your ability to keep up with your work duties or daily responsibilities, beyond just feeling internally low?

Yeah. At work, I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client documentation because I’m missing details. And at home, my wife’s taken over some of the bills and scheduling since I haven’t been as reliable with that stuff lately.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a two-week history of pervasive, persistent low mood, anhedonia-adjacent flatness, cognitive fog/concentration difficulty, disturbed sleep, fatigue, and passive suicidal ideation, all causing functional impairment at work and home. Although onset followed the death of his uncle, the symptoms extend beyond typical grief reactions—being present most of the day nearly every day, not limited to reminders of the loss, and including passive death wishes and significant functional decline. This symptom burden and pervasiveness meet criteria for a major depressive episode rather than uncomplicated bereavement or adjustment disorder, though the temporal link to a stressor and relatively short duration (2 weeks) leave adjustment disorder and normal bereavement as differentials to reconsider if symptoms remit or fail to meet full criteria on follow-up.
